title: SAML PHP Toolkit (onelogin/php-saml) vulnerability in xmlseclibs — SAML signature verification bypass (breaks Zabbix SAML SSO)
summary: Reviewed entry in the GitHub Advisory Database for the onelogin/php-saml package used by the Zabbix Frontend for SAML SSO. A vulnerability in the xmlseclibs dependency (CVE-2025-66475) lets an attacker exploit incorrect canonicalization/signature verification to bypass Digest/Signature verification of the SAML response and forge authentication. Zabbix fixed it by updating php-saml to 4.3.1 (in ZBX-27819). Only relevant to Zabbix when SAML SSO is enabled.
prerequisites: SAML SSO enabled on the frontend
Zabbix uses the bundled php-saml

public_poc.notes: No public PoC found; vulnerability in a dependency library (xmlseclibs), CVE-2025-66475

impact: Forged SAML response and SSO authentication bypass (access as an arbitrary user) if the attacker can control the SAML IdP response or intermediate traffic.
notes: CVE partner: php-saml has no CVE of its own (CWE-1395, dependency); associated with CVE-2025-66475 (xmlseclibs 2.x/3.x) and GHSA-c4cc-x928-vjw9 (CVE-2025-66578). GHSA record for php-saml: <2.21.1, >=3.0.0 <3.8.1, >=4.0.0 <4.3.1. Zabbix versions are affected via the bundled dependency: no exact per-branch threshold published for Zabbix, bounds taken from the fix versions in ZBX-27819 (max exclusive: versions up to 6.0.44/7.0.23/7.4.7 are vulnerable).

title: robrichards/xmlseclibs: Libxml2 canonicalization flaw bypasses XML Digest/Signature verification (used by Zabbix SAML SSO)
summary: Reviewed entry in the GitHub Advisory Database for robrichards/xmlseclibs (CVE-2025-66578): a Libxml2 canonicalization flaw allows XML Digest/Signature verification to be bypassed. xmlseclibs is a dependency of onelogin/php-saml, which Zabbix uses for SAML SSO; Zabbix addressed it by updating php-saml (ZBX-27819).
prerequisites: SAML SSO enabled
Zabbix uses the bundled php-saml/xmlseclibs
impact: Bypass of XML (SAML Assertion) signature/digest verification, potentially forging a SAML response and bypassing Zabbix SSO authentication.
notes: CVE partner: CVE-2025-66578 (xmlseclibs <=3.1.3, fixed in 3.1.4). Affects Zabbix only via php-saml (linked with GHSA-5j8p-438x-rgg5 / CVE-2025-66475). Zabbix versions bounded by the ZBX-27819 fix, max exclusive.

title: Open redirect (URL Redirect) via the request parameter in index.php
summary: The request parameter in index.php allows specifying an arbitrary external URL to redirect to. An attacker can use this for phishing (a malicious link like /zabbix/index.php?request=http://fakepage/). Ticket closed as duplicate — fixed as part of ZBX-13133 ("Multiple security issues in frontend").

public_poc.notes: PoC in the ticket description (malicious request parameter)

impact: Phishing: a user following a link to a legitimate Zabbix lands on an external malicious site.
notes: Fix released in ZBX-13133 (ticket without the security label); per-branch bounds taken from ZBX-13133 fix versions, max exclusive.

title: DoS: unvalidated stime parameter in charts.php makes the web server consume 100% CPU
summary: The stime parameter in charts.php is not validated: an incorrect value (e.g., 20000000160127113255) hangs the web server at 100% CPU (the _getdate() function returns an unexpected result). Not reproducible on Windows; on Linux — unbounded CPU consumption.

public_poc.notes: PoC string in the ticket description

impact: Denial of service of the frontend web server (high CPU load) when a specially crafted request to charts.php is sent.
notes: No CVE assigned. Authentication requirements not clarified in the ticket; charts.php usually requires a session (auth listed conservatively as user). Max exclusive.

title: CSRF: screen structure modification via GET requests (adding/removing rows and columns)
summary: The add/remove row and column actions in screen editing are performed via GET requests (screenedit.php). Simply giving the victim a link (or pressing F5) triggers the action — classic CSRF. Fixed by switching to POST forms and SID validation.

public_poc.notes: Example URLs in the ticket description

impact: Modification of screen configuration (up to corrupting monitoring data) for an authorized user without their knowledge.
notes: No CVE assigned. Max exclusive.

title: Media type password (SMTP etc.) returned in plain text in the settings form HTML
summary: A password set in media type settings (e.g., SMTP authentication) is rendered in plain text in the settings page HTML. Fixed in the same manner as ZBX-6721 (LDAP): the stored password is not returned to the browser, only replacement is possible.
prerequisites: Access to media type settings (Admin)
impact: Disclosure of a secret (SMTP/media password) in the page HTML; risk from shoulder-surfing, caches, proxy logs.
notes: No CVE assigned. Max exclusive.

title: LDAP users automatically created with Zabbix Administrator status (won't fix)
summary: With LDAP authentication, auto-created users are added to the Zabbix Administrators group (usrgrps=7 in CUser.php). All LDAP users get full access to configuration, including changing authentication settings. Vendor closed as "won't fix" (discussion points to configurability via ZBXNEXT).
prerequisites: LDAP authentication enabled
impact: Every LDAP user gets administrator rights — a serious weakening of the permission model when an external IdP is connected.
notes: Behavior by design (won't fix); branch range not confirmed (relevant for 2.x–3.x; newer branches allow configuring the group at auto-creation). Not to be confused with a CVE.

title: Built-in user parameter mysql.size[] executes unexpected shell commands (ash/dash) — CVE-2016-4338
summary: userparameter_mysql.conf (mysql.size[]) uses [[ ]] syntax that breaks on ash/dash (Debian) and allows passing arguments as commands (e.g., mysql.size[,uname] executes uname). Risk is limited, but these are commands run as the agent. The ticket comment says to use CVE-2016-4338.
prerequisites: Agent with the built-in mysql.size[] template (affects versions with a dash shell)

public_poc.notes: command examples in the ticket description

impact: Execution of arbitrary OS commands as the agent process via the mysql.size[] key when passing parameters (only on systems with dash/ash).
notes: CVE partner: CVE-2016-4338 (named in the ticket discussion). Max exclusive.

title: WASA: stored XSS via javascript: URLs in maps/triggers/user URL + CSRF in user creation
summary: NSOC WASA findings: (1) stored XSS — javascript:alert() can be placed in a map element URL, JS executes on click; (2) CSRF — user creation without reliable protection. The vendor added URL validation for map fields, triggers, and the user "after login" URL.
prerequisites: Ability to configure map/trigger URLs (Admin)

public_poc.notes: PoC: javascript:alert() in a map element URL

impact: Arbitrary JS execution in the victim's session (session theft, actions as the administrator) when opening an infected map.
notes: No CVE assigned. Two findings in the ticket (XSS + CSRF); type set to the primary one. Max exclusive.

title: Multiple reflected XSS in the frontend (popup.php, screen.import.php, etc.)
summary: Reflected XSS in several frontend pages: popup.php (injection into onclick via srcfld2), screen.import.php (backurl=javascript:), and others. A maliciously crafted link leads to JS execution in the user's context.

public_poc.notes: Several PoC links in the ticket description

impact: Arbitrary JS execution in an authenticated user's session (cookie theft, actions on their behalf).
notes: No CVE assigned. Max exclusive.

title: Guest has access to the script execution link (host data disclosure)
summary: Guest (and any unauthenticated user when guest is enabled) can open /scripts_exec.php?hostid=…&scriptid=… and, by tampering with the ids, obtain confidential information (e.g., the host IP). scripts_exec.php lacked permission checks.
prerequisites: Guest account enabled (enabled by default in older versions)
impact: Disclosure of confidential host information (IP etc.) accessible via global scripts; without authentication.
notes: No CVE assigned; the 2.2 branch is not affected (removed from fix versions). Max exclusive.

title: Reflected XSS in the popup form (popup.php)
summary: Reflected XSS in popup.php via the srctbl/srcfld1/dstfld1 parameters: injection of l')(alert(...)) into the template. JS executes when clicking any list item. Fixed by escaping values in popup.

public_poc.notes: PoC link in the ticket description

impact: Arbitrary JS execution in the user's session when following a crafted link.
notes: No CVE assigned. Max exclusive.

title: CSRF protection bypassed via the SID in the URL (session surfing)
summary: The SID is passed in the URL and is always the same (part of sessionId, not a surrogate). An attacker with guest access creates a screen with a URL element (iframe), reads the referrer containing the parent's SID, and having obtained the SID performs CSRF attacks (e.g., user creation) via session surfing. Fixed by removing the SID from the URL and hardening checks.
prerequisites: Guest user enabled (scenario from the ticket); the victim must visit the attacker's page

public_poc.notes: Full PoC (~45 lines of JS) described in the ticket

impact: Performing privileged actions (user creation etc.) as the victim without their knowledge — effectively a CSRF protection bypass.
notes: No CVE assigned. Max exclusive.

title: Stored XSS in IT Services + unauthorized IT service creation via the API
summary: The IT service name is not escaped: the injected JS executes when the service is deleted/viewed from the frontend (persistent XSS). Additionally, creating an IT service via the API required no special permissions — the combination makes the XSS available to unprivileged users.

public_poc.notes: PoC: service name with HTML/JS injection

impact: Stored XSS: JS execution in the sessions of all users opening IT services; plus unauthorized service creation.
notes: No CVE assigned. Max exclusive.

title: Stored XSS in the "map navigation tree" widget
summary: The widget element name of the "map navigation tree" widget is not escaped: executes on render. Persistent XSS in dashboards.
prerequisites: Ability to create/edit widgets (Admin)
impact: JS execution for all users when opening a dashboard with an infected widget.
notes: No CVE assigned. Max exclusive.

title: Missing autocomplete="off" in the user edit form (open)
summary: Cosmetic/hygiene issue: the user password change form lacks autocomplete="off", so the browser offers to save the password (risk on shared machines). Ticket open since 2018, no fix.
impact: Minimal: passwords may be saved by the browser's password manager on shared machines.
notes: Open (Open), no fix; range unknown.

title: User password leak into the media type passwd field via browser autofill
summary: A hidden but not disabled SMTP media type password field is autofilled by the browser with the user's saved password, which is sent to the API and stored in the DB (media table, passwd field) — the user's password ends up in plain text in an unexpected place. Fixed by disabling hidden password fields and rejecting API requests containing the password when authentication is disabled.
prerequisites: Browser with the user's saved credentials

public_poc.notes: reproduction steps in the ticket description

impact: Storage of the user's password in plain text in the DB (media type passwd field) — secret disclosure when viewing the DB/dumps.
notes: No CVE assigned. Max exclusive.

title: Zabbix version number accessible to unauthenticated users via the jsLoader URL
summary: Since 3.0 the version was not shown on the login page to prevent information leakage, but the version remained available to unauthenticated users via the jsLoader URL (as part of the JS loading path). Fixed by removing the version from the URL.
impact: Disclosure of the exact Zabbix version to unauthenticated users — simplifies version-based exploit selection.
notes: No CVE assigned. Max exclusive.

title: Command injection via the HOST.CONN macro in global scripts
summary: The HOST.CONN macro (as well as HOST.IP, IPADDRESS, HOST.DNS) is expanded in a global script command without validation: the host IP can be set to "127.0.0.1; cat /etc/zabbix/zabbix_server.conf" and the command will execute on the server. Fixed by validating the expanded macro (IP/domain only).
prerequisites: Global script using HOST.CONN/macros in the command
Ability to set the host IP/DNS

public_poc.notes: PoC with macro injection in the ticket description

impact: Execution of arbitrary OS commands on the Zabbix server when a global script runs (e.g., ping).
notes: No CVE assigned. Max exclusive.

title: Lowering the PCRE recursion limit to protect against stack overflow (DoS mitigation)
summary: The PCRE recursion limit was 1000000 — insufficient to protect against stack overflow. A user with preprocessing configuration rights could send a value via zabbix_sender and crash the server (stack overflow). The limit was lowered and is now computed based on the process stack limit.
prerequisites: Permissions to configure preprocessing rules with regexp
Ability to send data via zabbix_sender
impact: Protection against denial of service of the Zabbix server via PCRE stack overflow during preprocessing.
notes: No CVE assigned; this is a mitigation (latent DoS). Max exclusive.

title: Broken peer certificate issuer/subject verification on TLS connections: verification always succeeds
summary: For TLS connections between components (server/proxy/agent, zabbix_get/sender) with TLSServerCertIssuer/TLSServerCertSubject configured, the configured restrictions were not verified — the check "always succeeded". An attacker with a valid certificate from a trusted CA but a different issuer/subject could impersonate a legitimate peer. Incoming connection verification and cases without issuer/subject are unaffected.
prerequisites: TLSConnect=cert + TLSServerCertIssuer/TLSServerCertSubject configured
Attacker has a certificate from a trusted CA

public_poc.notes: reproduction steps in the ticket (a server with a foreign issuer/subject is accepted)

impact: Weakened component authentication: connection of an untrusted peer (e.g., a fake agent/proxy) while issuer/subject verification is enabled, MITM-like scenarios.
notes: No CVE assigned (not mentioned in the ticket). Max exclusive.

title: "Authentication bypass" via application/x-www-form-urlencoded (won't fix — guest behavior)
summary: Exploit-db 47474/post firo: with Content-Type application/x-www-form-urlencoded, authentication appears to be bypassed on many pages (dashboard.view etc.). The vendor clarified: the pages are accessible because the guest account is enabled; requests run as guest. Closed as won't fix; starting with 5.4 guest is disabled by default (ZBXNEXT-5532).
prerequisites: Guest account enabled (default in older versions)
impact: Unauthenticated access to data/pages visible to the guest user (system information, problems, etc.). Not exploitable when guest is disabled.
notes: Per the vendor's conclusion this is not a vulnerability but a consequence of enabled guest (won't fix). Included conditionally, since it was published as an auth-bypass.

title: Passwords printed to Zabbix Docker container logs
summary: Zabbix Docker containers print environment variables containing passwords (DB_SERVER_ROOT_PASS etc.) to logs at startup. Risk when logs are shipped to SIEM/centralized logging. Fixed by masking passwords with asterisks.
prerequisites: Use of official Docker images

public_poc.notes: example log output in the ticket description

impact: Disclosure of DB passwords in container logs (risk when logs are aggregated/stored).
notes: Closed Fixed, but the exact fix version is not specified in the ticket (fixVersions empty) — fixed_versions left empty, ranged_versions unknown.

title: Stored XSS due to a URL validator regression (macros in trigger/map URLs)
summary: Regression after the ZBX-12825 refactor (CHtmlUrlValidator): URL validation aborts when some conditions are met. javascript:alert() + a macro "salt" (e.g., //{$THIS.SHOULD.LOOK.LIKE.USERMACRO}) passes validation. The XSS fires in problems (trigger URLs), dashboard widgets, maps (inventory macros), and context menus.
prerequisites: Ability to set trigger/map element URLs

public_poc.notes: two PoCs (trigger and map) in the ticket description

impact: Stored XSS in key monitoring pages (problems, maps): JS execution in user sessions.
notes: No CVE assigned. Max exclusive.

title: Agent 2 debug level exposes secret texts configured in the frontend
summary: At debug level 5, agent 2 logs the values of secret texts (passwords/tokens) configured in the frontend. Ticket status "Elaborating" (effectively unfixed; Won't Fix noted in the discussion). Recommendation — restrict access to the logs.
prerequisites: Debug level 5 enabled on Agent 2
Access to the agent log file
impact: Leak of secrets (DB passwords, tokens) used by monitoring through agent logs at high debug verbosity.
notes: Open (Elaborating), no fix; range unknown.

title: Media type passwords in plain text in the audit log (UI and auditlog_details)
summary: When notification events fired, media type passwords were written in plain text to the audit log (UI and the auditlog_details table). Fixed by masking the password with '*' characters in the audit log.
prerequisites: Audit log readers
impact: Disclosure of media type passwords (SMTP etc.) in the audit log and DB — if logs/DB leak, secrets are in plain text.
notes: No CVE assigned. Max exclusive.

title: PSK key visible to administrators (not super-admins) after host auto-registration
summary: A PSK key set in auto-registration settings (visible only to Super Admins) is displayed in plain text in the host configuration (Encryption) after host auto-registration, which is also available to regular Administrators. Fixed by hiding the PSK in the API/host settings.
prerequisites: PSK auto-registration in use

public_poc.notes: reproduction steps in the ticket description

impact: Disclosure of the PSK key to administrators who are not allowed to see it in Administration — reduces trust in TLS-PSK.
notes: No CVE assigned; fix only in the 5.4 branch. Max exclusive (versions before the 5.4 fix are vulnerable).

title: Windows agent looks for openssl.cnf in c:\openssl-64bit — local privilege escalation via DLL hijacking
summary: The Zabbix Windows Agent (builds with OpenSSL) accesses the non-existent c:\openssl-64bit directory at startup. A local user can create it and plant a malicious openssl.cnf to load a DLL that executes with SYSTEM privileges (service). Fixed in newer builds; for older branches the best practices documentation was updated.
prerequisites: Windows agent built with OpenSSL (including 5.0.2 x64)
Local unprivileged user access to the file system
impact: Local privilege escalation to SYSTEM by tampering with the OpenSSL/DLL configuration (persistence, full host control).
notes: No CVE assigned. fixed_versions listed as 5.4.0 (fixVersions='5.4 (plan)'); no fix for 3.0-5.2 — best practices documentation only.

title: web.page.get: no domain name size limit — stack overflow in punycode_encode_part()
summary: punycode_encode_part() places a 2048-byte buffer on the stack and writes into it from a codepoints array without size checks. The function is reachable via the web.page.get item (and similar). Potentially a process crash/stack overflow with a specially crafted domain name.
prerequisites: Ability to create/edit web items or call web.page.get (regular user)
impact: Server process crash (DoS) / potentially unsafe stack overflow when processing a long domain name.
notes: No CVE assigned (based on the ticket and an NVD search for web.page.get). Max exclusive.

title: Update of the bundled jQuery (patch 753d591aea) — jQuery XSS fixes
summary: A jQuery patch (commit 753d591aea698e57d6db58c9f722cd0808619b1b) was added to the frontend, closing known XSS vulnerabilities in the jQuery library itself (including jQuery.parseHTML/HTML injections — CVE-2015-9251 and similar upstream issues). No Zabbix vulnerability of its own — a dependency issue.
impact: Closing jQuery's own XSS vectors across all frontend pages; before the fix, vulnerable jQuery functions could be used in combination with other XSS injections.
notes: No CVE assigned to Zabbix (issue in the jQuery dependency; related jQuery CVEs are not Zabbix). Max exclusive.

title: Java Gateway and Log4j (CVE-2021-44228): not affected, no fix required (won't fix)
summary: Log4Shell check of the Java Gateway: Zabbix Java Gateway uses logback 1.2.3, not log4j 2.x; the vendor confirmed CVE-2021-44228 does not affect the Java Gateway. Ticket closed as won't fix. A vulnerability in logback itself was identified separately — see ZBX-20383 / ZBA-2021-12-4.
impact: None (Java Gateway does not use log4j); entry included for completeness of the 2021 Log4Shell incident picture.
notes: Not a vulnerability; related to ZBA-2021-12-4 / ZBX-20383 (logback).

title: Possible remote code execution in the Java Gateway with logback 1.2.7 and older (CVE-2021-42550)
summary: The Zabbix Java Gateway ships with logback 1.2.7-and-older: an attacker with rights to edit configuration files (logback.xml) can create a malicious configuration that loads arbitrary code from LDAP servers — RCE. Corresponds to CVE-2021-42550 (logback). The logback update was delivered in 4.0.37/5.0.19/5.4.9/6.0.0beta2.
prerequisites: Rights to edit /etc/zabbix/zabbix_java_gateway_logback.xml (zabbix user)
Ability to restart the Java Gateway

public_poc.notes: no public PoC for the Zabbix build found; CVE-2021-42550 (logback) has attack descriptions

impact: Loading and execution of arbitrary Java code from LDAP/HTTP at Java Gateway startup/configuration reload — full compromise of the Java Gateway host, if the attacker already has rights to edit the configuration (requires privileges).
notes: Official advisory ZBA-2021-12-4 (Zabbix has no CVE number of its own; associated with CVE-2021-42550 — a CVE of the logback package, not Zabbix, so the entry stays in the non-CVE domain). The vendor rates severity as medium: exploitation requires privileges to edit the configuration. The 2.0/3.0 ranges are EOL, no fix; maxima exclusive. Workaround: read-only rights on logback.xml.

title: Auto-login cannot be disabled centrally (risk with external LDAP authentication)
summary: The auto-login setting is configured in the user profile and enabled by default; with LDAP this means that even after the account is removed in LDAP, the user can keep logging in via cookie for up to 30 days. There is no way to disable auto-login system-wide. Ticket closed as Confirmed (without a fix).
prerequisites: External (LDAP) authentication
impact: Session extension after account revocation in the external IdP (up to 30 days) — risk on offboarding/revocation of rights.
notes: Confirmed, no fix; range unknown (relevant for 6.0+).

title: Memory leak in the JSON parser (DoS)
summary: A memory leak in the JSON parser found during an audit (description hidden for security reasons). Repeated processing of JSON data (e.g., by preprocessing) leads to growing memory consumption and potential denial of service.
prerequisites: Ability to send/process JSON data (preprocessing, API)
impact: Server memory exhaustion — DoS.
notes: Description hidden (_Hidden due to security reasons_); details and CVE attribution not confirmed. Max exclusive.

title: Hang with a replace expression where pattern equals replacement (DoS)
summary: An expression where the pattern matches the replacement (e.g., in preprocessing/calculated items) causes processing to hang (infinite loop/high load). Fixed in 6.0.17/6.4.2. Description closed for security reasons.
prerequisites: Permissions to configure expressions/preprocessing
impact: Item processing hang — local DoS (blocks the data processing flow).
notes: Description hidden; CVE not confirmed. Max exclusive.

title: Crash when testing an item with an invalid calculated item expression
summary: Some forms of an invalid calculated item expression cause a crash (likely a server process/segfault) when testing the item. Fixed in 6.0.18/6.4.2. Description hidden for security reasons.
prerequisites: Ability to test item expressions
impact: Process crash — denial of service.
notes: Description hidden; CVE not confirmed. Max exclusive.

title: TLS: no Subject Alternative Name (SAN) check when validating component certificates
summary: Peer certificate verification between components compares only the configured CN string (TLSServerCertSubject) and does not support SAN. This is non-standard and creates operational gaps: administrators are forced to weaken/disable subject verification or issue shared certificates. Ticket Confirmed (essentially an improvement request).
prerequisites: TLS certificate-based authentication between components
impact: Operational weakening of PKI (practices of disabling subject verification or using shared certificates); not a directly exploitable vulnerability.
notes: Confirmed (improvement request labeled security); no fix.

title: php-saml update to 4.3.1 due to GHSA-5j8p-438x-rgg5 (SAML SSO)
summary: Zabbix updated the bundled onelogin/php-saml to 4.3.1, closing GHSA-5j8p-438x-rgg5 (SAML PHP Toolkit vulnerability in xmlseclibs, CVE-2025-66475) — a SAML signature verification bypass. The fix landed in 6.0.45/7.0.24/7.4.8/8.0.0beta1.
prerequisites: SAML SSO enabled
impact: SAML SSO bypass (authentication forgery) when exploiting GHSA-5j8p-438x-rgg5.
notes: Ticket partner of GHSA-5j8p-438x-rgg5 (see the separate entry). Max exclusive.

title: CVE-2016-9140: RCE via the JSON-RPC API (script.update + script.execute)
summary: Reported via the Debian BTS: an attacker with an Admin account can execute arbitrary commands on the Zabbix server via the API (script.update, then script.execute). Corresponds to CVE-2016-9140; public exploit-db 39937 exists.
prerequisites: Account with script permissions (Admin)
impact: Remote command execution on the server with Admin privileges.
notes: CVE partner: CVE-2016-9140 (details in the CVE research). Max exclusive.

title: CVE-2020-11800: RCE on the Zabbix server (trapper)
summary: Fixed CVE-2020-11800 (remote code execution on the server, found by FU CHUANG). Affected: 3.2 (EOL), 3.0 before 3.0.30, 2.2.x after 2.2.18 (EOL); 3.4/4.0/5.0 are not affected. The RCE executes only on the server (not the agent).
prerequisites: Access to the server trapper port (10051)
impact: Remote code execution on the Zabbix Server with access to the trapper port.
notes: CVE partner: CVE-2020-11800. auth listed as none based on the nature of the CVE (unauth trapper RCE); not explicitly stated in the ticket.

title: CVE-2020-15803: stored XSS in the URL widget (iframe without sandbox)
summary: The URL widget (dashboards) displayed content from a URL without the iframe sandbox attribute; the default Zabbix configuration allowed an unsafe iFrame. Fixed by adding the sandbox attribute by default (CVE-2020-15803).
prerequisites: URL widget on a dashboard
impact: Third-party page in an iframe without sandbox — XSS vector and phishing risk in the Zabbix context.
notes: CVE partner: CVE-2020-15803. Max exclusive.

title: CVE-2017-5929: serialization vulnerability in the logback shipped with the Java Gateway
summary: The Java Gateway shipped with logback-core 0.9.27.jar, affected by CVE-2017-5929 (serialization in SocketServer/ServerSocketReceiver). logback updated as part of the Java Gateway distribution.
prerequisites: Use of logback SocketServer/ServerSocketReceiver components (non-default configuration)
impact: Potential RCE when logback network components are enabled (serialization); the standard Zabbix configuration does not use them.
notes: CVE partner: CVE-2017-5929. Max exclusive.

title: CVE-2021-27927 (part 1): CControllerAuthenticationUpdate controller not protected by a CSRF token
summary: The authentication settings update controller called disableSIDValidation in init() and did not check the CSRF token. An attacker knowing the Zabbix URL and having contact with a user with sufficient rights could make them reconfigure authentication (CVE-2021-27927).
prerequisites: The administrator must follow a link crafted by the attacker
impact: CSRF: reconfiguration of authentication parameters (e.g., disabling verification/tampering with settings) in the administrator's session.
notes: CVE partner: CVE-2021-27927 (jointly with ZBX-19150). Max exclusive.

title: CVE-2021-27927 (part 2): audit and restoration of SID validation across all controllers
summary: Full audit of all controllers and non-MVC pages for CSRF token (SID) validation after ZBX-18942; validation restored where it was missing (CVE-2021-27927).
impact: Elimination of CSRF vectors across the entire frontend.
notes: CVE partner: CVE-2021-27927 (jointly with ZBX-18942). Max exclusive.

title: CVE-2023-29449: uncontrolled memory allocation and log writing from server-side JS
summary: Server-side JavaScript (JS preprocessing/script items) allowed allocating large amounts of memory and writing to the log, providing a controllable resource load (CVE-2023-29449). Restricted via Duktape limits.
prerequisites: Ability to create items with JS preprocessing/scripts
impact: Controlled memory/log consumption — potential DoS by a user with configuration rights.
notes: CVE partner: CVE-2023-29449. Ranges per the official advisory (from the Zabbix typesense collection).

title: CVE-2023-29452: removed ability to use HTML in the geomap attribution field
summary: The attribution field of the geomap configuration (Administration) allowed inserting HTML; it is now rendered as text without HTML for custom providers (CVE-2023-29452).
prerequisites: Custom geomap provider
impact: HTML injection (potential XSS) into geomap pages by an administrator; resolved by rendering as text.
notes: CVE partner: CVE-2023-29452. Max exclusive.

title: Some Zabbix products are affected by CVE-2022-3786 and CVE-2022-3602 (OpenSSL 3.0.0–3.0.6)
summary: Official notice: if the OS uses OpenSSL 3.0.0–3.0.6, Zabbix components are affected by CVE-2022-3786/CVE-2022-3602 (buffer overrun, DoS/potential RCE in X.509). Zabbix Solaris binaries and packages were rebuilt with OpenSSL 3.0.7 (as of November 1, 2022). Systems with OpenSSL 1.1.1–1.0.2 are not affected.
